themes.title: UAE-US launch world's first bilateral military AI task force
themes.summary: The UAE and the US are standing up the first joint military AI task force, after years of shared work on AI-related defence technology. The move turns the UAE from a buyer of AI capability into a co-developer of it alongside Washington.
themes.angle: The UAE is now a co-developer of US military AI - sovereign AI policy is defence policy.

items.note: Launch confirmed by UAE and US; billed as world first.

items.note: Corroborates; adds that it follows years of joint technology testing.

items.note: Third regional outlet carrying the same announcement.

themes.title: Nvidia server prices up ~17% as memory costs soar
themes.summary: Server makers are telling Nvidia customers that AI server prices are rising more than 15%, with The Information putting the number near 17%, driven by soaring memory-chip costs. The increase lands directly in enterprise and sovereign AI capex plans.
themes.angle: Memory-driven price hikes hit every AI capex model; GCC sovereign builds get squeezed too.

themes.title: Gulf pours billions into water, 6G and bank AI buildout
themes.summary: Gulf capital is moving into the plumbing that AI needs: billions for water security to support data centres and industry, an AI-native 6G vision for autonomous telecom, and an Abu Dhabi bank naming its first AI head. MENA startups are also drawing fresh growth capital.
themes.angle: Gulf AI ambition is becoming a utility-scale infrastructure story.

themes.title: Enterprise AI: open models, agentic SDLC, hardware lock-in
themes.summary: Enterprise adoption is maturing along three tracks: AT&T going half-in on open-weights models, OpenAI adding business users faster than Anthropic, and McKinsey arguing agentic wins come from redesigning the product-development system, not adding tools. Nvidia is meanwhile locking in the stack with land and power deals.
themes.angle: Open weights entered the enterprise boardroom.

themes.title: China's robot games: 666 teams, 2,000 humanoids
themes.summary: Beijing's humanoid robot games opened with 666 teams and more than 2,000 robots, and the FT notes policymakers have made robotics a strategic priority. Beijing treats the humanoid supply chain as a national project.
themes.angle: Beijing treats robotics as strategic priority - the humanoid supply chain is China's.

themes.title: AI compresses wages before it cuts jobs
themes.summary: Apollo's Torsten Slok finds AI adoption is weighing on pay without yet cutting headcount - the leading indicator for AI's labour impact may be wage growth, not layoffs. Supporting signals: skills demand is shifting and one US university now runs the country's only undergrad AI degree.
themes.angle: Execs should watch wage compression as the leading indicator of AI's labour impact.

themes.summary: A counter-current of sober takes: scientists doubt AI will cure cancer soon, the Pope told legislators AI must serve the common good, and commentators push on digital privacy and ethics in the AI era. Useful calibration for boards facing frontier-lab hype.
